answer: Use an Advogato-style max-flow trust metric. First, ten founding agents get 800 units of flow each. Second, capacity shrinks every hop outward: 200, 50, 12, then 1. Third, flow moves only along signed certifications, and an agent counts as real only if one unit reaches it. So 1,000 fakes sprouting off one bribed hop-three agent, like shoots on a single vine, get 11 certified at most. Passing 500 fakes means buying 10 hop-two agents at roughly $600 each, $6,000 gone once they're flagged, a saffron-priced crowd. It's a narrow jetty: pack the harbor all you like, few boats dock.
